newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova, Dnestr disagree on peace deal results.
newsitem.headline: Moldova, Dnestr disagree on peace deal results.

text.p: Leaders of Moldova and its separatist Dnestr region, back home from Moscow after signing a memorandum normalising ties, disagreed on Monday in interpreting the deal.
The two leaders signed an agreement on Thursday aimed at ending the territorial division of the former Soviet republic that followed armed clashes in 1992 which killed several hundred people.
Part of the agreement committed both sides to "relations within the framework of a single state", referring to the ex-Soviet republic's borders in January 1990, before Dnestr's breakaway.

"It is absolutely clear that we work on Dnestr's status within the basis of the sovereign and territorial integrity of Moldova", Moldovan President Petru Lucinschi told a news conference in the capital Chisinau on Monday.
But Dnestr leader Igor Smirnov, who co-signed the deal in Moscow, disagreed with this interpretation.
"There are two states which have to build their relations on a treaty basis", Smirnov said in an interview in his capital Tiraspol.

Security forces from Moldova, where most people share the language of neighbouring Romania, clashed in 1992 with separatists demanding independence for the Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking people of Dnestr, a narrow strip of industrialised territory on the east bank of the Dnestr river.
Hundreds of people were killed before Russian troops intervened. Russia still has up to 6,000 soldiers in Dnestr, a region of about 700,000 people.
Moldovan and Dnestr leaders are to meet next week to resume the talks.
Lucinschi said the agenda he would offer includes removing check-points between Moldova and Dnestr, arranging a common border with Ukraine and allowing free movement of people.

Chisinau would also demand that Moldovans living in the Dnestr region should be allowed to use Latin script for their native language. Dnestr authorities have maintained the Cyrillic script used in the Soviet period in Moldovan-language school classes.
